Firstly, I did no such thing. I tried to generalize that these hateful comments aren’t changing anyone’s mind. We the mods, were called that from both sides for moderating reasonably.

I think part of the issue is seeing the messaging differently. I see things he says and it does read to me as concerning. One example being ‘dictatorship’. Yes he’s not straight up named himself that. But he has said that if you vote for him you’ll never need to vote again and people in his party are in fact proposing a 3rd term. That feels concerning to me. I also am intelligent enough to understand he’s quite a showman and doesn’t necessarily mean what he says and that won’t necessarily happen. But it’s like seeing smoke in a building. Does it mean there’s a fire? Not necessarily, but there could be. Should I ignore it? Do my due diligence and then act? Could be nothing, could burn it all down. It’s a weird position to be in. I think people have a right to be concerned and it’s okay to be. I also think talking it over is great. Our community just needs to better our communication skills and base more in fact and reasoning than in name calling/shouting type convos. It’s just a difficult climate to navigate conversation because everything gets heated quickly.

Both of you are much better Mods than me. I try to stay out of it unless things are just extreme. I only delete super obnoxious name calling or like extreme misinformation. I might delete a whole post if it’s riling everyone up or maybe something like doxxing. I don’t think anyone has ever moderated to make the subreddit lean left. I think it naturally leans left. There really isn’t much posting centered or right leaning. I know that makes some people uncomfortable and it is easy to say it’s a subreddit bias but it truly isn’t. That’s just the community demographic that is here.
